The soil is washed away, and new plants cannot grow there.
Acid rain damages vegetation and trees. It can make soil too acidic for plants to grow; when trees are destroyed, soil is washed away and new plants may not grow.
Burning sulphur-containing fossil fuels releases SO₂. It can be oxidized to SO₃, which reacts with water to form H₂SO₄; these acids return to the ground in acid rain and other forms of precipitation.
